all.title: Filter profiles
all.intro: The profiles below organize the list by the predominant glucose pattern in the analyzed period. They work as a visual triage and do not replace clinical assessment.

sections.title: In-Range Profile
sections.body: Groups patients who did not reach the hyperglycemic or hypoglycemic profile thresholds. In the app's metrics, the reference range considers 70 to 180 mg/dL for general readings, 80 to 130 mg/dL for pre-meal readings, and values below 180 mg/dL for post-meal readings.

sections.title: Hyperglycemic Profile
sections.body: Applied when the period's average glucose is 185 mg/dL or higher, or when time in high is 65% or higher. Time in high considers readings at or above 130 mg/dL in pre-meal measurements and at or above 180 mg/dL in post-meal measurements or without specific context.

sections.title: Hypoglycemic Profile
sections.body: Applied when time in low is 10% or higher in the period. Time in low considers readings below 70 mg/dL.

sections.title: When both criteria are met
sections.body: The Hyperglycemic profile takes precedence: the patient is placed there and, in the list, the profile notes that they also spend 10% or more of readings below 70 mg/dL.

stable.title: In-Range Profile
stable.intro: This filter shows patients who stayed outside the hyperglycemic and hypoglycemic profile criteria in the current screening.

sections.title: Reference range
sections.body: The reference used in the metrics considers 70 to 180 mg/dL for general readings, 80 to 130 mg/dL for pre-meal readings, and values below 180 mg/dL for post-meal readings.

sections.title: How the filter applies here
sections.body: The patient stays in this group when the period's average glucose is below 185 mg/dL and time in low is below 10%.

attention.title: Hyperglycemic Profile
attention.intro: This filter highlights patients with a predominance of elevated readings in the analyzed period.

sections.title: Classification threshold
sections.body: The profile is applied when the period's average glucose is 185 mg/dL or higher, or when time in high is 65% or higher.

sections.title: What counts as high
sections.body: Time in high considers readings at or above 130 mg/dL in pre-meal measurements and at or above 180 mg/dL in post-meal measurements or without specific context.

oscillation.title: Hypoglycemic Profile
oscillation.intro: This filter highlights patients with a more significant recurrence of low readings in the period.

sections.title: Classification threshold
sections.body: The profile is applied when time in low is 10% or higher in the period.

sections.title: What counts as low
sections.body: Time in low considers readings below 70 mg/dL.

landing.title: Welcome to MyGlico
landing.desc: Glycemic tracking with clear and continuous insights.

hero.title: Your glucose, closely followed
hero.body: MyGlico keeps your readings, highlights what fell outside your pattern, and comes with Glico, an assistant that logs everything for you. Your doctor only sees what you authorize.
hero.badgeControl: You decide who sees your data
hero.mascotAlt: Glico, the MyGlico mascot, waving and giving a thumbs up

patient.title: Follow your own glucose
patient.body: See your indicators, log new readings and invite your doctor to follow along. You can revoke that access whenever you want.

doctor.title: Follow those who trust you
doctor.body: Receive link requests, see only the dashboards patients authorized and answer their questions in one place.

glico.title: Talk to Glico, it logs for you
glico.body: Type the value, send a photo of your meter's display or record a voice note. Glico shows what it understood and only saves after you confirm.
glico.bot: Logged 112 mg/dL, today at 7:40 AM. Save it?

indicators.title: Indicators that tell how your days went
indicators.body: Average, time in the 70 to 180 mg/dL range and how the period evolved, in charts that are easy to read. The numbers support the talk with your doctor; they are not a diagnosis.
indicators.chartAlt: Example chart with readings across a week, most of them inside the 70 to 180 mg/dL range

atypical.title: Atypical days, no scare
atypical.body: MyGlico highlights the days that broke your pattern. For each one you can open a clarification and talk it through with your doctor.

report.title: A PDF report, ready for the appointment
report.body: Pick the period and download a report in Portuguese, English or Spanish to bring to your doctor.

consent.title: You decide who follows you
consent.body: Every link with a doctor is an invitation from you, and you can revoke it whenever you want.

cta.title: Ready to start?

glicoAssistant.clarifyImage: I could not read the glucose safely from this photo. Try a sharper, straight-on photo of the display or type the value, such as “110 mg/dL”.

howLog.q: How do I log a reading?
howLog.a: Write the value with the unit (e.g. 110 mg/dL), send a photo of the display or record audio. You review and confirm before saving.

privacy.q: What happens to my photos and audio?
privacy.a: They are read once to suggest the value and then discarded. Only the reading you confirm is stored.

where.q: Where do I see my readings?
where.a: On the dashboard, which shows charts, indicators and reading history.

advice.q: Does Glico say what dose to take?
advice.a: No. Glico does not diagnose or advise on treatment; talk to your doctor.
